messages:
raj: quick heads-up, saw a regression on the AWQ INT8 weight-only path after the batching heuristic tweak this morning. p50 looks ok but p95/p99 spiked for small-seq chat workloads. link: https://perf.redwood/reports/2310001234
amy: ugh. which heuristic change? the "prefer-batch" switch?
raj: yeah, the change prefers 4-8 request batching for low-latency tier. It seems to cause extra pack/unpack churn for weight-only kernels when group_size != 32
chris: numbers?
raj: profiling snapshot: throughput down ~12% for group_size=64 on A100, p99 latency +27ms, KV cache miss rate up from 3% -> 18% for the sample trace (convos with many short prefixes)
olivia: interesting. so batching increases packing calls and evicts kv cache entries? can you paste the perf trace snippet?
raj: pasted below:
```
# perf summary
kernel: awq_int8_w_only_pack  time 58.2ms (was 46.1ms)
kernel: awq_int8_infer      time 120.3ms
kv-cache: hit_rate 82% -> 68%
pack_cpu: 0.9ms/request -> 2.4ms/request
memmove: +1.1GB/s sustained
```
raj: also saw more small-malloc churn in allocator traces, likely due to canonical buffer alignment when packing 4-bit vs 8-bit groups
amy: memory alignment + group_size 64 could be causing larger scratch buffers, and our kernel-selector might be choosing an AWQ kernel variant that expects contiguous packed buffers, forcing extra copies
chris: did the kernel selector change? I thought it only looked at seq_len & batch_size, not group_size
raj: we updated it to include `prefer_batch=true` heuristics which bumped the threshold for preferring the serial kernel to the batch kernel. apparently the batch kernel triggers a different pack layout (more intermediate buffers)
tj: @raj can you repro with GPTQ quantized weights? AWQ's pack format is a bit heavier since it stores scales and zeros per group
raj: good call. ran same workload with GPTQ weights: throughput drop was ~3% instead of 12%, pack_cpu only went to 1.3ms/request
olivia: that suggests AWQ pack layout + the new batching path combine to amplify packing cost. AWQ likely has per-group metadata that increases copy work
perf-bot: automated-alert: regression-detected on eng-ml/awq-int8 path (regression_id: r-2310-01)
chris: plan: 1) bisect the batching heuristic revert vs kernel-selector revert 2) try a kernel fallback that avoids packing for batch_size<=4 or seq_len<=64 3) run group_size sweep (16/32/64) with both AWQ & GPTQ
amy: also test prepack cache — if we memoize packed weights per model version *and* group_size, we avoid runtime pack cost at inference time. downside: memory blowup for many group sizes
raj: did a quick prepack sim: memory +12% but pack_cpu drop to 0.2ms/request in the hot path. For many customers that might be acceptable.
tj: can we do a hybrid: prepack for group_size<=32 and dynamic pack for larger groups? most production models use 32 or 16
olivia: worth exploring. Also check the KV eviction policy: the increased pack time could be lengthening request processing which in turn holds KV cache locks longer causing evictions under the slab allocator. Look at `kvcache.hold_time` traces
raj: captured kvcache traces: hold_time median +9ms during batched bursts, eviction_count doubled
chris: timeline: revert heuristic -> verify p99 back to baseline -> if not, revert kernel-selector tweak. If revert fixes it, we need a better simulation test to catch this in CI
amy: I'll put together a small regression test that simulates chat-style short-prefix traffic and validates p99 latency delta < 5% across quant variants
raj: for immediate mitigation, can we ship a config toggle `pack_on_write=true` to prepack models at load time for the hosted infra? That avoids customer impact while we fix selector
tj: Ops flagged memory concerns for multi-tenant hosts. We need an opt-in rollout and a mem cap
olivia: notes for follow-up: - profile memmove hotspots (likely memcpy in pack) - instrument kernel-selector decision path with reasons - add prepack mem-estimator in console - add regression test in perf harness
chris: assigning tasks: amy -> regression test; raj -> bisect and kvcache traces; olivia -> memmove hotspot & prepack sim; tj -> ops rollout plan and toggle; I'll own the kernel-selector fallback patch
amy: ack, will open PR with test + baseline numbers
raj: thanks all, moving to bisect now, will post small repro link when done: https://perf.redwood/repro/2310001234/repro.tar.gz
chris: :thumbsup: keep thread updated
perf-bot: note: created ticket INF-2310 (priority P2) linking this thread
